stageLabels: 🎫 Exit · receive and use the response

sequence.title: Enzyme Action: Preparing the pH Investigation
sequence.outcome: Edexcel GCSE Biology 1BI0 Foundation · Paper 1 · Topic 1 · enzyme action, pH and Core Practical 1.10 preparation.
sequence.objective: I can explain enzyme specificity and denaturation, then identify the variables and evidence needed to investigate the effect of pH on amylase safely.

sequence.title: Amylase and pH: Continuous-Sampling Investigation
sequence.outcome: Edexcel GCSE Biology 1BI0 Foundation · Paper 1 · Topic 1 · specification point 1.10 investigation of pH and enzyme activity.
sequence.objective: I can follow the centre-approved Pearson method to investigate how pH affects amylase activity, recording safe continuous-sampling evidence accurately.

sequence.title: Amylase Rate, Graph and Topic 1 Consolidation
sequence.outcome: Edexcel GCSE Biology 1BI0 Foundation · Paper 1 · Topic 1 · rate calculation, CP 1.10 analysis and Topic 1 consolidation.
sequence.objective: I can calculate amylase rate from endpoint time, plot and interpret the pH pattern, evaluate the method, and apply Topic 1 knowledge to exam-style evidence.

sequence.title: Cell Cycle: Copy, Check, Divide
sequence.outcome: Edexcel GCSE Biology 1BI0 Foundation · Paper 1 · Topic 2 · specification point 2.1 · the cell cycle and mitosis.
sequence.objective: I can describe the cell cycle, distinguishing interphase from mitosis and cytokinesis, and sequence prophase, metaphase, anaphase and telophase using chromosome evidence.

sequence.title: Mitosis Sequence: Chromosome Evidence
sequence.outcome: Edexcel GCSE Biology 1BI0 Foundation · Paper 1 · Topic 2 · specification point 2.1 · mitotic sequence and chromosome evidence.
sequence.objective: I can identify and sequence stages of the cell cycle from diagrams or micrographs, justify stage decisions with visible chromosome evidence, and evaluate uncertainty in snapshot data.

sequence.title: Mitosis: Identical Daughter Cells
sequence.outcome: Edexcel GCSE Biology 1BI0 Foundation · Paper 1 · Topic 2 · specification points 2.2–2.4 · identical daughter cells, roles of mitosis and uncontrolled cell division.
sequence.objective: I can explain how mitosis produces two genetically identical daughter cells with the parent chromosome number, then apply the process to growth, repair, asexual reproduction and cell-division data.

sequence.title: Growth and Differentiation: Building an Organism
sequence.outcome: Edexcel GCSE Biology 1BI0 Foundation · Paper 1 · Topic 2 · specification points 2.5–2.7, growth and cell differentiation in animals and plants.
sequence.objective: I can describe how animals and plants grow and explain how differentiation produces cells specialised for particular functions.

sequence.title: Stem Cells and Meristems: Potential Compared
sequence.outcome: Edexcel GCSE Biology 1BI0 Foundation · Paper 1 · Topic 2 · specification point 2.8, embryonic and adult animal stem cells and plant meristems.
sequence.objective: I can compare embryonic stem cells, adult tissue stem cells and plant meristem cells using evidence about self-renewal, differentiation range and function.

sequence.title: Growth and Stem-Cell Data: Evidence Before Claims
sequence.outcome: Edexcel GCSE Biology 1BI0 Foundation · Paper 1 · Topic 2 · specification points 2.5–2.9, growth data, differentiation and stem-cell applications.
sequence.objective: I can interpret growth and stem-cell data, calculate changes or proportions, and evaluate application claims using evidence and biological limitations.

sequence.title: Stem Cells: Evidence Before Judgement
sequence.outcome: Discuss potential benefits and risks associated with the use of stem cells in medicine.
sequence.objective: I can describe stem-cell functions and distinguish scientific evidence, ethical concern and uncertainty.

sequence.title: Stem-Cell Evidence: Benefit, Risk, Uncertainty
sequence.outcome: Discuss potential benefits and risks associated with the use of stem cells in medicine.
sequence.objective: I can analyse simulated stem-cell evidence by calculating outcomes and identifying benefits, risks and limitations.

sequence.title: Stem Cells: Structured DISCUSS
sequence.outcome: Discuss potential benefits and risks associated with the use of stem cells in medicine.
sequence.objective: I can write or dictate a structured DISCUSS judgement and improve it after feedback.

sequence.title: Genetic Information: Cell to Gene
sequence.objective: I can describe where genetic information is stored and how chromosomes, DNA, genes and the genome are related.

sequence.title: DNA Structure: Pair, Twist, Critique
sequence.outcome: Describe DNA as a polymer of nucleotides arranged as two strands coiled into a double helix, with complementary base pairs joined by weak hydrogen bonds.
sequence.objective: I can construct a complementary DNA section and describe the strengths and limitations of the model.

sequence.title: Fruit DNA: Extract, Observe, Evaluate
sequence.outcome: Explain how DNA can be extracted from fruit; connect the observation to genetic information.
sequence.objective: I can explain the steps in fruit-DNA extraction, record an observation and evaluate the evidence cautiously.

sequence.title: Inheritance Language: Allele to Phenotype
sequence.outcome: Explain monohybrid inheritance using genetic diagrams and Punnett squares.
sequence.objective: I can use inheritance vocabulary to connect alleles, genotype and phenotype in a simple monohybrid model.

sequence.title: Punnett Squares: Construct the Prediction
sequence.outcome: Explain monohybrid inheritance using genetic diagrams and Punnett squares.
sequence.objective: I can construct a Punnett square from parental genotypes and explain what its outcomes predict.

sequence.title: Inheritance Data: Predict, Calculate, Evaluate
sequence.outcome: Calculate and analyse outcomes using probabilities, ratios and percentages from monohybrid crosses.
sequence.objective: I can calculate inheritance probabilities, ratios and percentages and evaluate why observed results can differ from predictions.
